title: ✏️ Short Answer Questions

sections.heading: What it tests
sections.body:
Short answer questions ask you to answer in your own words — or more often, using words directly from the passage. The key constraint:

"Answer using NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS from the passage"

This means:
• You copy words FROM the passage (do not paraphrase)
• You use EXACTLY the number of words stated
• A number counts as one word ("2,500" = one word)
• Hyphenated words count as one word ("well-known" = one word)

sections.heading: Technique
sections.body:
1. Read the question carefully — what specific thing is it asking?
2. Identify the question's keywords and scan the passage
3. Find the answer location — slow down and read carefully
4. Extract only the words you need — no extras
5. Grammar check: does your answer fit grammatically in the question?

highlight: "No more than three words" means 1, 2, or 3 words are all acceptable. The most precise answer is usually best.

title: 🔢 Word Count Rules
body:
These rules catch many students out:

✅ "climate change" = 2 words
✅ "well-established" = 1 word (hyphenated)
✅ "2.5 million" = 2 words (number + noun)
✅ "CO2" = 1 word (abbreviation)

❌ "the climate change" = 3 words (unnecessary article adds a word)

Tip: Articles (a, an, the) count as words. Remove them if they push you over the limit — usually the meaning is clear without them.

question: The question says "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS." The answer in the passage is "the rapid industrialisation." What should you write?
explanation:
"The rapid industrialisation" = 3 words (the + rapid + industrialisation).

Removing "the" gives "rapid industrialisation" = 2 words ✅

Articles (the, a, an) can almost always be dropped from answers without changing the meaning. This is the most common short-answer error.

question: A question asks "What did scientists discover?" The passage says: "Scientists found that excessive screen time adversely affects cognitive development in children under five." What is the best short answer (max 3 words)?
options: screen time adversely affects cognitive development
explanation:
"What did scientists discover?" = "What was found?"
The discovery was: excessive screen time affects "cognitive development"

"Cognitive development" (2 words) directly answers the question.

"Excessive screen time" answers WHY, not WHAT was discovered.
"It adversely affects development" is a full clause — too long.
hint: The question asks for the THING discovered, not the cause.

sentence: In short answer questions, you should use words _______ from the passage, not your own paraphrase.
explanation:
Unlike essay writing where you paraphrase, short answer questions require you to use the EXACT words from the passage.

This is the opposite of what you do in Writing Task 2.

"Directly" is the most precise answer here. "Taken" and "copied" also work but "directly" is the most standard instruction.

question: Which answer correctly follows the "NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS" rule for: "What method did the study use?" when the passage says "The study employed a longitudinal data collection methodology"?
explanation:
"Longitudinal data collection methodology" = 4 words ❌ too many
"Longitudinal data collection" = 3 words ✅
"A longitudinal study" = 3 words ✅ but less precise
"Data collection" = 2 words ✅ but misses "longitudinal"

Best: "longitudinal data collection" — most precise within the word limit.
